properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's principles document (art:storyflow-engineering-principles), whose closing note states the case better than a summary can: "Structure alone found none of these. The leverage of a graph is not tidiness — it is that a graph CAN bind each rule to an executable check and then report which rules have none."

MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN, 2026-08-22. 19 DesignRules. 16 have NO Verification pointing at them. Of those 16, only 3 are `enforced: true` — and `unverified_enforced_rule`, the detector that exists, fires ONLY on enforced rules. So 13 unchecked rules are structurally invisible: written down, checked by nothing, and never mentioned again.

THE SHAPE IS fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it, one level up. There it was optional FIELDS staying empty because no detector noticed their absence. Here it is whole RULES, and the same enforced-only blind spot that hid change_axis_unstated hides these.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) Widen `unverified_enforced_rule` to all rules. Simple, and it turns 3 findings into 16 overnight on this design alone — probably too loud, and loud-on-day-one is how a whole category gets filtered forever.
(b) A separate AGGREGATE finding: "N of M rules have no check" — one question, one acknowledgement, the shape `change_axis_unstated` and `unreviewed_ideas` already use. Naturally quiet, and it asks exactly the question the document says is the point.
(c) Require a rule to state WHY it has no check, rather than to have one. The document's own note says "this rule has no detector and here is why" is a legitimate end state — so the finding becomes not "you lack a check" but "you have neither a check nor a reason".

⭐ (c) IS THE INTERESTING ONE and it is not obvious. It reframes the goal: not that every rule is automated — several of these nine explicitly cannot be — but that no rule is SILENTLY unautomated. That is the distinction review_relations already makes for ideas, where a written note is a full answer and not a weaker one.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded rather than resolved: reflow2 has an accepted non-goal that it does not judge whether a check is MEANINGFUL. Reporting that a rule has no check at all stays the right side of that line — an absence, not a quality judgement — but (c) edges closer, because "is that reason good enough?" is precisely the judgement the non-goal refuses.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 report a rule that nothing checks, including the UNENFORCED ones? 13 of this design's 19 rules are invisible to the detector that exists
properties.rationale: Recorded because the measurement is concrete and the blind spot is the same one this session already fixed once for change events. Not proposed as intent because (a), (b) and (c) are a real fork with different costs, and because it may be subsumed by the governing question about whether reflow2 ships rule machinery at all.
